title: Epistola Fidei Catholicae In Difensione Trium Capitulorum
author: Facundus of Hermiane
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1125.tmp1125.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Si enim mortuos quos damnaverunt prave docuisse et hæretico sensu libros conscripsisse dicunt, quærimus ab eis utrum cum vivcrent admoniti sint juxta morem catholicæ observantiæ ac disciplinæ, ut sanum rectumque saperent, pertinaciter restiterint, convictiquede errore suo, vcl in aliquo concilio accersiti, ut Arius in N - cæno, Maccdonius in Constantinopolitano, Nestorius in Ephesino primo, Eutyches atque Dioscorus in Chalccdonensi, condemnati fuerint necne. Si factura dixe- rint, mox ferri synodalia gesta flagitaverimus, sicut horum proferuntur, ubi condemnatus eorum error, ubi prolata adversus eos sententia doccatur.
passages.english: For if they say that the dead men whom they have condemned taught wrongly and wrote books in a heretical sense, we ask them whether, while they were alive, they were admonished according to the custom of catholic observance and discipline to think soundly and rightly, whether they stubbornly resisted, and whether, convicted of their error, or summoned to some council, as Arius was at Nicaea, Macedonius at Constantinople, Nestorius at the first [council] of Ephesus, Eutyches and Dioscorus at Chalcedon, they were condemned or not. If they say it was done, we will at once demand that the synodal acts be brought forward, just as those of these men are produced, where it may be shown that their error was condemned and where sentence was pronounced against them.
passages.notes: Several scanning errors corrected silently (vivcrent = viverent, vcl = vel, N - cæno = Nicaeno, Maccdonius = Macedonius, Chalccdonensi = Chalcedonensi, doccatur = doceatur). 'convictique de' read as two words. 'Si factura dixerint' is odd; read as 'factum' ('that it was done'). 'Ut sanum rectumque saperent' taken as the content of the admonition; 'pertinaciter restiterint' lacks a connective in the Latin and is rendered as a further question.

passages.original: I Hæc interim pro brevitate prolata sufficiant testimonia, quoniam si amplius coacervare vel ratiocinari vellemus, legentium forsitan memoriam oneraremus. Nunc jam illud quoque breviter commemorare debemus, quod ex beati Augustini opusculis contra Donatistas scriptis obji iunt, dicentes: Dixit sanctus Augustinus : Bona esl pax, habete pacem; bona est finitas, diligite unitatem, non scindatur unitas. Sed hæc et talia egregii doctoris testimonia, quantum eos supp'odant, nos vero stabiliant, nequa- quam perspiciunt.
passages.english: For the sake of brevity, let these testimonies brought forward suffice for the present, since if we wished to pile up more or to argue further, we might perhaps burden the memory of our readers. Now we must also briefly mention what they raise as an objection from the little works of blessed Augustine written against the Donatists, saying: "Saint Augustine said: Peace is good, keep peace; unity is good, love unity; let unity not be torn apart." But they by no means perceive how much these and similar testimonies of the eminent teacher undercut them and indeed strengthen us.
passages.notes: The initial "I" appears to be a stray mark or initial from the printed page and is omitted. Scanning errors corrected: "esl" for "est", "finitas" for "unitas" (required by "diligite unitatem"), "obji iunt" for "objiciunt", "nequa- quam" for "nequaquam". "supp'odant" is unclear; read as "suppedant" or "supplantant" (undercut, trip up), in contrast to "stabiliant" (strengthen).
